title: The IRC test client must answer the server's PING
description: The test client in crates/mimid-agent/tests/common/irc.rs reads the socket only when a test calls next(), and never answers a PING. A test that waits on the store instead of on a line -- burn_and_expire_from_irc waits twice for the expiry loop to delete a message -- says nothing on its connection for as long as that wait takes, and the front end closes it with 'ERROR :Closing Link (Ping timeout)' after DEFAULT_PING_AFTER plus DEFAULT_PONG_WITHIN (90 s + 90 s). The next read then finds the connection gone: 'closed before the short-lived line'. Seen in a full-suite run of 2026-11-27 with twelve test binaries at once; the test passes alone. The front end is behaving correctly: a client that never answers is dead.
design: A reader task owns the read half and the writer behind a mutex, so the connection answers PING while the test is waiting on anything else, as a real client does. The PING is answered and not forwarded, so a test reads only the lines it asked about, and the front end clears its keepalive on any line received. Irc::drop aborts the task, so dropping the connection still closes the socket. Regression test over tokio::io::duplex: write a server PING into the socket and assert the PONG comes back before the test reads a line.
